```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

## Problem 1

```{r load-penguins}
data("penguins", package = "palmerpenguins")
```

The penguins dataset contains measurements of penguins from the Palmer Archipelago in Antarctica. It has `r nrow(penguins)` rows and `r ncol(penguins)` columns. Important variables include species (`r paste(levels(penguins$species), collapse = ", ")`), island (`r paste(levels(penguins$island), collapse = ", ")`), bill length and depth (mm), flipper length (mm), body mass (g), sex, and year.

The mean flipper length is `r round(mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE), 2)` mm, excluding missing values.

```{r penguin-scatterplot}
penguin_plot = ggplot(
  penguins,
  aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = flipper_length_mm, color = species)
) +
  geom_point(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Flipper length versus bill length",
    x = "Bill length (mm)",
    y = "Flipper length (mm)",
    color = "Species"
  )

penguin_plot

ggsave(
  filename = "penguin_scatterplot.png",
  plot = penguin_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```

The scatterplot shows the relationship between bill length and flipper length, with different colors representing the three penguin species. Penguins with missing measurements are omitted from the plot.
